column1: # SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE of screening/target_clades.tsv: the one thing needed to say
# whether an off-target amplicon came from INSIDE the target or from OUTSIDE it.
# The rows match examples/targets_example.tsv; replace them with your own.
# WHY IT EXISTS: MFEprimer's "off target" measure rests on product LENGTH
# alone. A universal bacterial primer finds hundreds of differently sized
# amplicons that all begin with "Bacteria;..." in SILVA, that is they are
# INSIDE the target and are the natural length polymorphism of 16S. Put into
# the verdict, the raw count would make such a pair come out risky. This table
# makes the distinction measurable.
# The columns:
#   hedef   the target name exactly as it stands in targets.tsv / the panel
#   alan    Bacteria | Archaea | Eukaryota  (the FIRST token of the SILVA lineage)
#           (b) same domain, outside the clade ; (c) another domain
#   klad    a comma separated token list. If ANY of them occurs in the
#           amplicon's taxonomy lineage the amplicon counts as INSIDE the target.
#   kaynak  where the tokens came from, so that the choice can be audited
hedef
Escherichia_coli_species
column4: targets.tsv decision 1, member 562; SILVA does not resolve below genus, so the genus token is used

column1: Bacillus_subtilis_species
Pseudomonas_genus
Lactic_acid_bacteria_group
column4: targets.tsv decision 3, the three genera plus their shared order

column1: Bacteria_universal
column4: targets.tsv decision 4, level 'alan': every taxon in class LIB1
